---
title: "Getting Started"
---

This chapter covers installation, a first model fit, and how to read the
output.

## Installation

### From CRAN

```r
install.packages("bgms")
```

### Development version

```r
if(!requireNamespace("remotes")) {
  install.packages("remotes")
}
remotes::install_github("Bayesian-Graphical-Modelling-Lab/bgms")
```

## Fitting a model

The main entry point is `bgm()`. It accepts a data frame of binary, ordinal,
continuous, or mixed variables and estimates a Markov Random Field.

The Wenchuan dataset, included in the package, contains ordinal posttraumatic
stress ratings from 362 survivors of the 2008 Wenchuan earthquake. We use a
five-item subset as a quick demonstration.

```{r}
library(bgms)

data(Wenchuan)
data = Wenchuan[, 1:5]
head(data)
```

```{r}
#| eval: false
fit = bgm(data, seed = 1234)
```

```{r}
#| include: false
fit = bgm(data, seed = 1234, chains = 2, display_progress = "none",
           verbose = FALSE)
```

By default, `bgm()` runs four parallel MCMC chains using the No-U-Turn
Sampler (NUTS), with Bayesian edge selection enabled. Here we use
`seed = 1234` for reproducibility.

## Posterior summaries

```{r}
summary(fit)
```

The summary shows posterior means, standard deviations, Monte Carlo standard
errors (MCSE), effective sample sizes (ESS), and R-hat values for each
parameter. For pairwise interactions, it also reports posterior inclusion
probabilities when edge selection is active.

## Posterior means

```{r}
coef(fit)
```

`coef()` returns posterior mean matrices: `$pairwise` contains the
interaction strengths and `$indicator` contains edge inclusion
probabilities.

## Network plot

To visualize the estimated network, threshold inclusion probabilities at 0.5
and plot the result using the qgraph package.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 7
library(qgraph)

median_probability_network = coef(fit)$pairwise
median_probability_network[coef(fit)$indicator < 0.5] = 0.0

qgraph(median_probability_network,
  theme = "TeamFortress",
  maximum = 1,
  fade = FALSE,
  color = c("#f0ae0e"), vsize = 10, repulsion = .9,
  label.cex = 1, label.scale = "FALSE",
  labels = colnames(data)
)
```

Edges with posterior inclusion probability below 0.5 are set to zero, so only
edges with at least moderate evidence of inclusion appear in the plot.

## Continuous data

For continuous variables, `bgm()` fits a Gaussian graphical model. Set
`variable_type = "continuous"`:

```r
fit_ggm = bgm(continuous_data, variable_type = "continuous", seed = 1234)
summary(fit_ggm)
```

The pairwise effects are partial correlations (off-diagonal entries of the
standardized precision matrix). Missing values can be imputed during sampling
with `na_action = "impute"`.
